title: Your pattern toolbox
idea: MEET: recall the handful of patterns you own — running total, count-with-condition, track biggest/smallest, average, filter, search — one of them fits most sub-problems.

exercises.prompt: Which pattern adds every item into one growing value?
exercises.explanation: A running total starts at 0 and adds each item. It's the go-to for 'what's the total?'.

exercises.prompt: Which pattern keeps only the items that pass a rule?
exercises.explanation: A filter walks the list and keeps (or collects) just the items matching a condition.

exercises.prompt: You already own patterns for total, count, biggest, smallest, average, filter, and search.
exercises.explanation: Yes — Laps 4 and 5 built all of these. Pattern selection is choosing the right one, not learning new ones.

exercises.prompt: Which pattern answers 'how many items pass a rule?'
exercises.explanation: A conditional count starts at 0 and adds 1 each time an item passes the rule.

exercises.prompt: Select the patterns you can already use.
exercises.explanation: The first three are real patterns from earlier laps. The last one isn't a thing.

exercises.prompt: Which pattern answers 'is this value present in the list?'
exercises.explanation: Search walks the list looking for a match and reports found or not found.

exercises.prompt: Match each pattern to what it produces.
exercises.explanation: Each pattern has a signature output. Recognising the output helps you pick the pattern.

exercises.prompt: Why keep your patterns in mind as a 'toolbox'?
options: Each sub-problem usually matches one familiar tool
exercises.explanation: Decomposition gives you sub-problems; the toolbox gives you a tool for each. Selection links them.

exercises.prompt: Order the step where patterns come in.
blocks: Pick a pattern for each sub-problem
exercises.explanation: Understand, split, THEN choose a pattern per part. Selection is the third step.

options: You own a small toolbox of patterns; selection picks the right one per sub-problem
You must invent a new pattern each time
exercises.explanation: A handful of patterns covers most sub-problems. This unit is about matching part to pattern.
